context.in_practice: Route 1 is supposed to refuse a file with exit 4 when the dash layout doesn't match the parsed items. This file has nested dashes, a dash alone on its line, and a comment after a dash, and route 1 still did not refuse it. Both routes gave the same result on every command, so this test never triggered the refusal.
context.stakes: A config file with an unusual but valid layout (nested dash lists, a dash alone on its line with the value below it, a comment right after the dash) must either be read and edited correctly or be refused. A silent misedit would damage the user's file. In this test both routes read and edited it correctly, and neither refused it.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 adds a load-time check that can refuse a file with exit 4, but nothing here triggered it. Route 2 has no such check, and it handled every layout tested correctly.

plan_why: The config uses unusual but valid block-sequence layouts: nested items on one line (`- - read`), a lone dash with its item on the next line, and a dash followed by a comment. Route 1 refuses to load this file and exits 4 on every command. Route 2 loads it, prints the values and writes changes into these lists.
routes: Block sequences whose dash layout does not match the parsed items exit 4
